launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.description: Music Concourse is the central arrival for the de Young, California Academy of Sciences, Japanese Tea Garden, fountains, garage, and transit.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.hours: The outdoor concourse follows park access, but every museum, garden, garage, and fountain uses its own schedule.

launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.description: Blue Heron Lake, formerly Stow Lake, circles Strawberry Hill with walking paths, bridges, boating, wildlife, and a separately operated boathouse.
Koret Children's Quarter is the park's major playground beside the historic carousel; ride and playground schedules are separate.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.hours: The outdoor play area and separately operated carousel use different posted hours; check the carousel schedule before promising a ride.

launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.description: The car-free JFK Promenade links the Conservatory of Flowers, gardens, art, seating, and east-side park destinations.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.hours: JFK Promenade follows park access, while the Conservatory of Flowers is ticketed and follows its own opening days and hours.

launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.description: The Bison Paddock and nearby Spreckels Lake form a quieter west-central wildlife and model-boating destination.
The Polo Field and western meadows serve cycling, field sports, festivals, and large events that can substantially change road access.
The Japanese Tea Garden is a separately operated historic garden beside Music Concourse with paths, bridges, a tea house, admission hours, and limited free-entry windows for San Francisco residents.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.hours: The Japanese Tea Garden follows seasonal admission hours that are shorter than Golden Gate Park hours; confirm the official schedule before visiting.

launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.description: San Francisco Botanical Garden is a separately operated 55-acre living collection with entrances near 9th Avenue and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, accessible routes, restrooms, and its own admission rules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.hours: The Botanical Garden follows seasonal admission hours that are shorter than Golden Gate Park hours; check the official visit page for today's last entry.

launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.description: Tunnel Tops combines the Outpost nature playground, Field Station, lawns, picnic sites, restrooms, food vendors, and bridge views.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.hours: Tunnel Tops, the Outpost, Field Station, food vendors, and restrooms use separate posted hours within the 24-hour Presidio grounds.

launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.description: Main Post and the Visitor Center are the best orientation base for maps, transit, museums, food, history, and current conditions.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.hours: The Presidio Visitor Center is generally open daily 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., except listed holidays; surrounding Main Post grounds remain accessible separately.

launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.description: Baker Beach has two free lots, restrooms at the north lot, picnic areas, Battery Chamberlin, cold surf, and dramatic bridge views.
Fort Point and nearby overlooks provide close Golden Gate Bridge views, historic interpretation, shoreline trails, wind, and separate facility hours.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.hours: Fort Point National Historic Site, its access gate, and nearby outdoor overlooks use different hours; confirm the NPS schedule before entering Marine Drive.

launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.description: Lovers' Lane and Wood Line form a forest walk through the south Presidio, away from the busier waterfront destinations.
Immigrant Point Overlook is a west-facing coastal viewpoint reached from Washington Boulevard, with paid roadside parking, wind exposure, and access toward the Batteries to Bluffs Trail.
El Polin Spring is a restored natural and cultural site with a boardwalk, picnic tables, habitat, and interpretation in the Tennessee Hollow watershed.
Rob Hill is San Francisco's only campground, a reservation-only group facility in the Presidio forest with separate access rules and no casual drop-in camping.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.hours: Rob Hill is reservation-only camping rather than a drop-in public attraction; access follows reservation and check-in instructions.

launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.description: Helen Diller Playground is the park's accessible family destination near Church and 20th Streets, separate from the broad social lawns.
The upper southwest lawn provides the signature skyline view and steepest grades, with heavy crowds on warm afternoons.
Tennis, basketball, multi-use courts, and the soccer field occupy the park's active-recreation zones and may be reserved or busy.
Lower lawns and two designated dog areas sit closer to 18th Street, Dolores Street, transit, and neighborhood businesses.
The soccer field occupies the active lower recreation zone and can be reserved or heavily used; dogs and casual picnics should remain outside active play.
Picnic Area D sits along the central promenade and can be reserved for gatherings; playground-side picnic tables have youth-event rules and separate time blocks.
The north off-leash area lies on the Dolores Street perimeter slope near the central promenade and is distinct from on-leash lawns and sports areas.
The south off-leash area is north of Helen Diller Playground, where owners must keep dogs controlled and out of the playground and nearby active field.

launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.description: Lands End Lookout and the Sutro Baths ruins are the primary western arrival, with restrooms, overlooks, stairs, wind, and slippery historic surfaces.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.hours: Outdoor overlooks and ruins follow posted park access, while Lands End Lookout and its restrooms have shorter staffed hours.

launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.description: The Coastal Trail reaches Mile Rock Beach by steep stairs and natural paths; cliff and surf conditions make this a more demanding route.
The USS San Francisco Memorial and adjacent overlook sit near the eastern Lands End trail, with broad ocean and Golden Gate views.
Fort Miley combines historic batteries, grassy picnic space, trail links, and access near the Legion of Honor.
Eagles Point is the eastern Lands End overlook near the Legion of Honor, offering Golden Gate views and a useful turnaround for shorter walks.
Mile Rock Overlook is a signed Coastal Trail viewpoint above the rugged shore; reaching Mile Rock Beach requires a separate descent of roughly 100 stairs.
Lands End Point is a lower rocky terrace reached from the Coastal Trail. The informal stone labyrinth has been repeatedly damaged and rebuilt, so its presence is never guaranteed.
Sutro Heights Park preserves the landscaped grounds and historic remnants above Ocean Beach, with broad lawns, cliff views, and paths separate from the Sutro Baths stairs.

launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.description: East Beach offers sand, accessible parking and restrooms, picnic tables, grills, drinking water, a seasonal beach mat, and a dog wash.
The generally level Crissy Field Promenade follows the bay past restored marsh habitat with mixed walking, running, and bicycle traffic.
West Bluff and the Warming Hut provide picnic space, restrooms, food when open, fishing access, and the closest base for Fort Point.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.hours: West Bluff remains an outdoor destination, while the Warming Hut cafe and staffed services use shorter independent hours.

launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.description: Torpedo Wharf and the Fort Point connection bring visitors close to deep cold water, fishing activity, bridge wind, and historic shoreline routes.
Crissy Field Center is an environmental education facility near East Beach with programs and its own opening schedule; it is not a general visitor center for all park services.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.hours: Crissy Field Center opens for scheduled programs and organization hours; do not assume it is open whenever the surrounding shoreline is accessible.

launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.description: Golden Gate Beach is the narrow western sand section below the bridge approach, closer to West Bluff and Fort Point than to the main East Beach facilities.
The former airfield lawn is the broad open grass between the promenade and Mason Street, used for informal recreation, picnics, events, and bridge views.
The restored tidal marsh has overlooks along the promenade; visitors should stay on developed paths and keep pets away from sensitive wildlife habitat.

launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.description: The Esplanade lawn and MLK Memorial waterfall form the main free garden landscape at 750 Howard Street.
The Children's Creativity Museum and historic carousel are separately operated family attractions south of Howard Street with their own fees and hours.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.hours: The Children's Creativity Museum and carousel use separate admission days and hours from the outdoor gardens.

launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.description: The Children's Garden and play circle add free outdoor play near the paid family attractions and use their own opening procedures.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.hours: The Children's Garden and play areas may use shorter opening hours than the surrounding gardens; confirm gates on arrival.

launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.description: The East Garden and surrounding paths connect public art, seating, cultural venues, convention activity, and downtown transit.
The historic 1906 LeRoy King Carousel operates beside the Children's Creativity Museum with separate tickets, height supervision rules, and Wednesday-through-Sunday hours.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.hours: The carousel is currently listed Wednesday and Thursday noon to 4 p.m. and Friday through Sunday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.; verify before visiting.

launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.description: The indoor Ice Skating and Bowling Center offers paid public skating, lessons, hockey, and 12 bowling lanes with schedules independent from the outdoor gardens.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.hours: Public skating, lessons, hockey, and bowling each follow the operator's daily schedule rather than the outdoor garden hours.

launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.description: Oche Wat Te Ou is a reflection garden and public artwork connected to the MLK Memorial area; maintenance can temporarily affect fountains and connecting paths.
The Upper Terrace and amphitheater overlook the Esplanade and host free performances and private events that can occupy seating or redirect normal circulation.

launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.description: The west-end amphitheater lawn and stage host frequent free fitness, music, film, and family programs and may be occupied by events.
The children's play area and fountains provide active family space on the rooftop, with operation affected by weather and maintenance.
The half-mile botanical loop passes 13 ecosystem gardens, benches, lawns, public art, and exposed rooftop viewpoints.
Five elevator banks, an escalator, and the plaza gondola connect the four-block park to the Transit Center and surrounding streets.
The Main Plaza at Mission and Fremont is the clearest street-level meeting point, with the gondola and a glass floor that brings light into the Transit Center.
The redwood garden is one of 13 labeled botanical zones along the rooftop loop, providing shaded seating among the surrounding towers.
The Bus Fountain is a motion-activated artwork whose jets respond to buses moving below; operation can pause for maintenance or weather.
The desert garden anchors the west end while the wetland garden occupies the east, making the full botanical walk nearly four blocks long.

launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.description: The Steiner Street edge provides the classic Painted Ladies and skyline view; it is an overlook, tour stop, and residential frontage rather than an attraction entrance.
The dual-level accessible playground is the park's primary children's destination, reached most accessibly from Hayes and Scott.
The designated off-leash dog area shares the hilltop park with lawns, paths, picnics, and heavy visitor traffic.
The tennis court and picnic lawn provide neighborhood recreation beyond the famous view, with hill grades and seasonal restroom hours.
The Hayes and Scott corner is the designated accessible entrance and the most useful arrival for the playground and developed interior paths.
The accessible public restroom closes earlier than the park, using longer spring and summer hours and an earlier fall and winter closing.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.hours: Restroom hours are 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in spring and summer and 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. in fall and winter.

launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.description: The hilltop walking loop connects the Painted Ladies view, gardens, lawns, playground, dog area, and tennis court but includes exposed slopes and busy crossings.
The north lawn offers neighborhood picnic space away from the busiest Steiner Street photo stop, with no guarantee of reservable tables or wind shelter.

launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.description: North Ocean Beach near Kelly's Cove and the Cliff House area is used for walking and experienced surfing, with cold water and powerful currents.
Legal seasonal fires are limited to provided rings between stairwells 15 and 20 from March through October and must end by 9:30 p.m.
The Sloat Boulevard area provides southern promenade and beach access near the end of Sunset Dunes, with changing road circulation.
The snowy plover protection area south of stairwell 21 has seasonal six-foot leash requirements and sensitive dune habitat.
Beach Chalet and the north parking area provide a recognizable arrival near Golden Gate Park, with nearby food and restrooms operating on separate schedules.
Fulton Street reaches the north-central beach near Golden Gate Park and Sunset Dunes, with parking and circulation affected by the car-free oceanfront layout.
Judah Street is a major Muni arrival for central Ocean Beach; identify the correct stairwell and restroom before crossing the broad promenade.
Taraval Street provides a southern transit and neighborhood approach to the beach, with widely spaced facilities and dangerous surf despite easy sand access.

launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.description: Lincoln Way is the north entrance connecting Sunset Dunes with Golden Gate Park and the north end of Ocean Beach.
Judah Street is a central activity hub for transit, skate and bike features, events, and the Shipwreck Cove installation area.
Noriega provides the current temporary restroom and a practical midpoint on the two-mile promenade.
Sloat Boulevard is the south entrance, connecting the car-free park with southern Ocean Beach and west-side transit.
The Lawton zone contains the skate space, bike skills course, pump track, exercise equipment, and a rock spinner in a busy mixed-speed section.
The Pacheco zone combines a nature exploration area, interactive art, seating, a drinking fountain, and the Noriega-area restroom nearby.
The Rivera zone provides hammocks, elevated surf-perch seating, and a quieter pause between active recreation areas, all exposed to wind and fog.
The Taraval zone includes another nature exploration area and access toward the south end; confirm current installations and construction before promising a specific play feature.
